chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf from Fadala ibn Ayub from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Fadhl from some of our companions from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
"There is no harm if the Muhrim (person in Ihram) enters the bathhouse, but he should not scrub his body."
And there is no harm in wearing weapons when fearing the enemy or otherwise; he narrated.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.يَتَدَلَّكُ: To scrub or rub the body vigorously

ai.seo_question: What are the rulings on bathing and wearing weapons for a Muhrim?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that the prohibition on scrubbing (*tadalluk*) in Ihram is specific to removing dead skin rather than general washing, allowing pilgrims to maintain hygiene in bathhouses. It further establishes the principle of *al-istihlal* (justification) for wearing weapons during Ihram when fear of enemies or other threats arises, balancing ritual purity with practical safety. These rulings reflect the Shia juristic emphasis on distinguishing between minor inconveniences and substantive violations of Ihram conditions.
